about: Divergences of the native `ah issue-intake` command from hooks/issue-intake.mjs. A row named under rowsExercisingNode is recorded from Node, run natively, and counted as diverged (never as a failure) when it differs; an xUnit row pins the native answer.
ruling: accepted by the Orchestrator (note 20261012): IN-1, IN-2 and IN-3 are named divergences; runtime-produced stack and error text cannot match V8/Node, and the {"error"} line and the exit code do match

divergences.about: The hook-errors.jsonl row a failed intake run leaves carries "stack": []; Node writes the first three V8 frames of the throw site (file:line:column inside issue-intake.mjs and node internals), which a native binary cannot reproduce. Hook name, message and every other field are identical.

The diagnostic of a snapshot write or stale-snapshot removal failure is the .NET exception's message where Node logs its errno text (`EACCES: permission denied, open '<path>'`). The printed {"error": ...} line is identical.

For a conventions file that is not JSON the conventions-invalid detail carries the shared Conventions library's parser message (System.Text.Json) where Node prints V8's; a file that parses but breaks the schema is worded identically. No recorded case exercises the unparseable form.

usageText: The usage text names `ah issue-intake` where Node prints `node issue-intake.mjs`; mapped by cli-form-intake-usage under the cli-command-form family (0114 4c). Option errors keep parseArgs' own words.
